notes.decision: Greek ἐπεί 'since, when' — opens the chapter as a conditional/temporal protasis. The whole opening describes the consequence-chain when wisdom withdraws.
Read as ⲥⲓⲛⲉ 'pass, depart' + ⲁ-ⲧⲉⲥ-ⲙⲁ 'unto her place.' Wisdom (fem.) departs from the brother to her own place — the standard Manichaean motif of light-faculties withdrawing when sin enters.
Lyc. ϩⲱⲣⲃ̄ 'lurk, lie hidden, be slowed.' Translated 'has lurked-hidden' — Wisdom's withdrawal becomes a state of concealed inactivity rather than total disappearance.
Final word of L1 unclear; tentatively 'behold(?)' from Coptic ⲉⲓⲉ 'well, lo.' Could continue into the lacuna-start of L2. Flagged for parallels.
Lyc. ⲙⲛⲧϩⲁⲣϣϩⲏⲧ 'patience, longsuffering' (lit. 'state of slow-heartedness'). Standard Coptic virtue-noun.
Read as ⲁ-ϫⲱϩ 'unto strife, vexation' (Sah. ϫⲱϩ 'touch, strike, vex'). Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ is regular. Fits the conflict-progression of the kephalaion.

Translated 'multitude'; Lyc. ⲁϣⲁⲓ 'be many, multiply,' substantivized. Could alternatively be 'half/half-portion.' The collocation 'smallness of heart and multitude of sin' fits standard moral diagnosis.

Translated 'foolishness' (= Sah. ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲟϭ/ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲟⲃⲉ). The opposition with ⲥⲩⲙⲃⲟⲩⲗⲓⲁ ('counsel') and ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ('Mind of Light'), combined with the result 'becomes a fight and war,' confirms the negative valence. NOT to be confused with ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching.'

Tentatively 'his threshing-floor' — Greek ἅλων (Coptic ϩⲁⲗⲱⲛ) with ⲣ for ⲗ. The threshing-floor is the standard Manichaean ecclesiological image for the gathered community where grain is separated. Alternative readings: 'his enclosure/company.' Confidence low.
Greek φορεῖν 'wear, bear (as garment).' Per accumulated vocabulary. Here used metaphorically: they 'wear' lust, slackness, haughtiness — vices as garments donned by the apostate brother.
Greek χαῦνος 'slack, loose, vain.' Translated 'slackness' — moral remissness, the opposite of patience.
Lyc. ⲙⲛⲧϫⲁⲥⲓϩⲏⲧ 'high-of-heart' = haughtiness, arrogance (cf. accumulated ⲝⲁⲥⲓϩⲏⲧ). Completes the vice-triplet lust/slackness/haughtiness.
Lyc. ⲟⲩⲁⲁⲧ-ϥ̄ 'alone, by himself.' The repeated emphasis 'alone' (lines 19, 20, 21) marks the apostate's isolation as the diagnostic sign of foolishness — anti-communal individualism.
ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ('one, single') = 'of a single sort.' The brother eats/drinks 'of a single kind' — refusing communal sharing of varied food.

Tentatively 'exhortation' from ⲧⲱⲃⲥ̄ 'urge, exhort, persuade.' Alternative 'embrace, kiss' (from ⲧⲁⲡ 'embrace'). The community-restorative sense fits 'the X of the brothers does not please him' — what fellow-brothers offer that the apostate now rejects.
ⲣ̄-ϩⲛⲁ-ϥ 'be pleasing to him' — standard Coptic 'please.' Negated by ⲙⲁⲡⲉ.

Greek ἐνθύμησις 'thought, deliberation' + 'of death.' In the five-faculty system ⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ corresponds to ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ 'counsel.' Here Sin lifts a death-counsel up to the brother's thought (ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ, 2nd faculty) — corruption rises through the faculties.
Tentatively 'in him' (= ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ⸗ⲉ̄ with unusual feminine/contracted suffix). Could be a relative form. Confidence low.
ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'fame, report, repute.' 'His fame is scattered in the church' — public knowledge of his apostasy spreads. Alternative 'his beauty' (ⲥⲁⲉⲓⲉ) less apt to context.
'The teachers of the church' (ⲥⲁⲃⲉⲩⲉ pl. of ⲥⲁϩ 'teacher'). The ecclesiastical office that intervenes for restoration — paralleling the apostolic ⲥⲁⲍ figure throughout the Kephalaia.

'The building of God' = the church as edifice. Pauline-Manichaean ecclesiological image; the goal of restoration is reincorporation into the divine architecture (cf. line 3 ⲡⲕⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉϩⲥⲛⲏⲩ 'the building-up of his brothers').

Lyc. ⲃⲱⲗⲕ 'be vexed, be angry,' substantivized as 'his vexation/anger.' The brother is rescued from his agitated/wrathful state through the brothers' counsel. Alternative 'his lack/poverty' (ⲃⲱⲱⲕⲉ) possible.
